Changed files (you may Read these and any other file in the repo):

  - pipeline/configs/e24bs4-poly-4k-env-only-qwen3-1_7b.yaml

+# SUPERSEDED by e24bs4-poly-4k-env-only-qwen3-1_7b.yaml. Do not run this one.
+# It trained on 2026-07-29, before a19b1ff made batch_size default to 4, so
+# runs/e24-poly-4k-env-only-qwen3-1_7b/ was produced at batch_size 1 and its
+# numbers are void. Running this file TODAY resolves batch_size to 4 and would
+# silently produce a different experiment under the same name.
 experiment_id: e24-poly-4k-env-only-qwen3-1_7b
 description: "E24: control arm for the raised-cap cosine test, cosine reward off. The e22 probe showed the 2048 completion cap was the confound behind the e9-e18 null: every episode that hit the cap terminates when given room (16/16 across poly and countdown, zero loops), and on polynomial_equations all four rescued episodes are CORRECT, taking the e12 checkpoint from 0.80 to 1.00 on the same seeds. The sweep was therefore scored on rollouts cut mid-reasoning, mislabelled wrong, and then handed to the cosine wrong-branch that pays for length. Budget here is 4096 (max_seq 5120 - prompt 1024), twice the old one and the hardware ceiling on a 24 GB L4: accelerate upcasts the completion logits to fp32 for the policy backward, so peak grows by 10 bytes per token per vocab entry (bf16 logits + fp32 copy + fp32 grad, vocab 151936) on top of a 14.4 GiB resident base. Measured OOMs at 16384, 7168 and 6144 fix that model; 4096 leaves about 1.4 GiB of margin. TRL 1.6 has no chunked-logp escape (use_liger_loss does not exist in this version), and the only way past this ceiling is dropping accelerate's mixed precision, which would break numeric comparability with every earlier run. 4096 covers 18 of the 20 correct-episode lengths the probe measured - the same 18 that 6144 or 7168 would cover, because nothing in the measured distribution falls between 3093 and 9516. Pairs with e25."
 seed: 42

Byte-identical to what produced runs/e24bs4-*. Why the cap is 4096 and not higher: the e22 probe showed the 2048 cap was the confound behind the e9-e18 null, since every episode that hit it terminates when given room (16/16 across poly and countdown, zero loops), and on polynomial_equations all four rescued episodes are CORRECT, taking the e12 checkpoint from 0.80 to 1.00 on the same seeds. The sweep was therefore scored on rollouts cut mid-reasoning, mislabelled wrong, then handed to the cosine wrong-branch that pays for length. 4096 (max_seq 5120 - prompt 1024) is the hardware ceiling on a 24 GB L4: accelerate upcasts the completion logits to fp32 for the policy backward, so peak grows by 10 bytes per token per vocab entry (bf16 logits + fp32 copy + fp32 grad, vocab 151936) on top of a 14.4 GiB resident base. Measured OOMs at 16384, 7168 and 6144; 4096 leaves about 1.4 GiB of margin. It covers 18 of the 20 correct-episode lengths the probe measured - the same 18 that 6144 or 7168 would cover, because nothing in the measured distribution falls between 3093 and 9516."
+seed: 42
+
+model:
+  slug: qwen3-1.7b
+  lora_r: 16
+  max_seq_length: 5120
+  gpu_memory_utilization: 0.23
+
+training:
+  mode: agentic
+  env: reasoning_gym

+

 experiment_id: e25-poly-4k-cosine-w16-qwen3-1_7b
 description: "E25: the cosine length reward's fair test, paired with the e24 control. Relative to e17 (same task, same weight 16, 2048 budget, null) the completion budget doubles to 4096, which is the hardware ceiling - see e24. That takes the share of truncated-and-mislabelled rollouts from about 20 percent to about 10 percent: the e22 probe measured correct-episode lengths of median 702, p90 3093, max 9877, and 18 of 20 fit under 4096. max_len is set to 4096 as well, which here is the right call rather than the earlier design error - the error was setting max_len to a cap far above where completions actually live, because the cosine is flat near both endpoints and the whole distribution would sit in the dead zone. At a 4096 cap the covered distribution spans 213 to 3093, i.e. 5 to 75 percent of the curve, so the reward has real slope across it. With the task near-saturated at this budget most groups are all-correct, so the env component has zero within-group variance and contributes nothing under advantage_weighted, and the cosine correct-branch drives the entire gradient - the best case the countdown pair was meant to supply before the graded-scorer artifact killed its premise. Watch accuracy: compression bought with correctness is the Wu/Yeo overshoot."

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

experiment_id: e24bs4-poly-4k-env-only-qwen3-1_7b
description: "E24bs4: control arm for the raised-cap cosine test, cosine reward off. Pairs with e25bs4, and the two together are the first comparison in this project free of both void causes - the completion cap is 4096 rather than 2048, and batch_size is 4 rather than the old silent default of 1. Recovered into configs/ from the frozen runs/e24bs4-poly-4k-env-only-qwen3-1_7b/config.yaml, which was the only copy: the pair was launched ad hoc on the box and its configs were never tracked, so the one clean comparison could not be re-run or seed-replicated. Byte-identical to what produced runs/e24bs4-*. Why the cap is 4096 and not higher: the e22 probe showed the 2048 cap was the confound behind the e9-e18 null, since every episode that hit it terminates when given room (16/16 across poly and countdown, zero loops), and on polynomial_equations all four rescued episodes are CORRECT, taking the e12 checkpoint from 0.80 to 1.00 on the same seeds. The sweep was therefore scored on rollouts cut mid-reasoning, mislabelled wrong, then handed to the cosine wrong-branch that pays for length. 4096 (max_seq 5120 - prompt 1024) is the hardware ceiling on a 24 GB L4: accelerate upcasts the completion logits to fp32 for the policy backward, so peak grows by 10 bytes per token per vocab entry (bf16 logits + fp32 copy + fp32 grad, vocab 151936) on top of a 14.4 GiB resident base. Measured OOMs at 16384, 7168 and 6144; 4096 leaves about 1.4 GiB of margin. It covers 18 of the 20 correct-episode lengths the probe measured - the same 18 that 6144 or 7168 would cover, because nothing in the measured distribution falls between 3093 and 9516."
seed: 42

model:
  slug: qwen3-1.7b
  lora_r: 16
  max_seq_length: 5120
  gpu_memory_utilization: 0.23

training:
  mode: agentic
  env: reasoning_gym
  env_config:
    dataset: polynomial_equations
    size: 500
  env_server:
    repo_path: /workspace/OpenEnv/envs
    port: 8077
  max_prompt_length: 1024
  # Geometry stated, never defaulted: freezing copies the config verbatim, so a key
  # no config writes is absent from the frozen copy and the e24bs4-vs-e25bs4 diff
  # cannot prove the arms matched. max_steps is 150 rather than e24's 300 because a
  # step at batch_size 4 costs four times as much wall clock; both arms of THIS pair
  # run 150, which is what the comparison requires.
  batch_size: 4
  n_rollouts: 8
  micro_batch_size: 1
  max_steps: 150
  learning_rate: 5e-6
  kl_beta: 0.001

rewards:
  compose_method: advantage_weighted
  env_reward:
    enabled: true
    weight: 1.0
  token_length:
    enabled: false

eval:
  temperature: 0.0
  do_sample: false
  agentic:
    n_episodes: 100

1	experiment_id: e25bs4-poly-4k-cosine-w16-qwen3-1_7b
2	description: "E25bs4: the cosine length reward's fair test, paired with the e24bs4 control. Recovered into configs/ from the frozen runs/e25bs4-poly-4k-cosine-w16-qwen3-1_7b/config.yaml, which was the only copy - see e24bs4. Differs from e24bs4 in exactly the rewards.token_length block and nothing else. Relative to e17 (same task, same weight 16, 2048 budget, null) the completion budget doubles to 4096, the hardware ceiling, which takes the share of truncated-and-mislabelled rollouts from about 20 percent to about 10 percent: the e22 probe measured correct-episode lengths of median 702, p90 3093, max 9877, and 18 of 20 fit under 4096. max_len is 4096 as well, which here is the right call rather than the earlier design error - that error was setting max_len far above where completions actually live, because the cosine is flat near both endpoints and the whole distribution would then sit in the dead zone. At a 4096 cap the covered distribution spans 213 to 3093, i.e. 5 to 75 percent of the curve, so the reward has real slope across it. With the task near-saturated at this budget most groups are all-correct, so the env component has zero within-group variance and contributes nothing under advantage_weighted, and the cosine correct-branch drives the entire gradient - the best case the countdown pair was meant to supply before the graded-scorer artifact killed its premise. Watch accuracy: compression bought with correctness is the Wu/Yeo overshoot. Read the pair's frac_reward_zero_std against e24bs4's before reading the result - 99.5 percent of groups are live here against 40.7 percent in the control, so the contrast is reward plus more gradient, not the reward alone."
